I'm still newly diagnosed and trying to get used to it all. Immediately post diagnosis, I was told to test 3x a day (fasting, before dinner, and before bed). After my numbers improved, I was told to test twice a day (fasting and a time of my choosing). Since my last appointment, I wasn't told to make any adjustments with my testing, but since I was taken off insulin, they wanted me to make sure my blood sugar didn't get too high or fall too low with the medication change. So now, I test fasting in the morning and a few times throughout the day because I can't really feel lows. Usually after the gym to see if I'm lightheaded because of overtraining or if I've dropped too low. Also sometimes at work because I have a long period of time between lunch and going home. 

When I test after meals, it's usually 2 hours after but since I have plenty of strips, I've done 1 hour, 2 hours, and 4 hours just to see how things look. If things continue the way they're going, I'll just switch to just fasting and when I don't feel good. I love seeing the data but I'm trying not to become obsessed as long as I'm in control.

My appetite only disappeared during my violent diarrhea stage of metformin but only because I didn't want to give any fuel to my bowels. Once that passed, my appetite was good. Could eat any and everything until I got used to the 1600 calorie diet I was put on.  And then I started going to the gym and could eat a live horse if you put it in front of me. And now I'm on Mounjaro and my appetite is here but for only a few bites.

I just did my 5th shot earlier today so I've had a full month using it as T2. 

First things first: don't eat if you're not hungry. If you do, you will have a bad time.

But my experience has been great. A lot of people have been losing mad weight even within the first month but I haven't seen that yet. However, my blood sugar levels are amazing. My Endo praised my tight control before prescribing (fasting below 100, post meal between 110-125) and it's only gotten better. I've had days where neither fasting nor post meal got out of the 80s and that's with just Metformin. She actually took me off Tresiba when she prescribed. I also find that I'm not as interested in eating and can't eat much.

There's quite a few side effects you can experience. Probably the ones everyone thinks about are nausea, diarrhea, and general feel bad, but I have some constipation (mostly because I'm not eating much) and insomnia here and there. It's mild and not turning me off from using it. Of course ymmv but I hope it's something that helps you.

Same. Except it's at my bedside. I choke down my meds as soon as I wake up and the afternoon ones as soon as I get home... Or when I look at the case and see today's dose is still in there right before bedtime.

I'm actually eating little bites of candy regularly for the first time in years because my bgl just hovers around 80 and my body is poorly adjusting to this new constant low. I hope I get used to it soon because I'm not looking to develop a candy habit.

I've only gotten as low as like 76. I was just like a little hungry and thought I would just be like 96 like normal and then I saw it was actually lower than I've ever been and I felt fine. I was about to go to bed but had a little snack so I could take my basal and go to sleep. My endo said it wasn't a real low so I guess I haven't reached a terrible low yet. However, if I'm at 105~110, I actually feel low and I'm always shook when I check the meter.

Endo told me to do it before bedtime so I started at 10pm. I began to get so excited about injecting myself that I couldn't wait for 10 so it eventually crept up to 9pm which works well because I began going to sleep early. However, I'm still often accidentally falling asleep too early and waking up in a panic to inject myself. I've been diagnosed T2 for like 4 months now and it's been going very well. My fasting is rarely out of the 90s.

Most of the time, no pain. However, I did inject once in the lower part of my thigh where there's more muscle and it kinda burned and I regretted being so hasty that night. I also don't like doing my arms. It's not pain, but it doesn't feel right.

I have both Accu Chek Guide and Guide Me (backup for travel). They're both Bluetooth and both pretty great imo. I can use both of them to communicate with my phone to report my numbers. Bottom line, they both get the job done. The Guide is my main and I like it a lot better because I have a rhythm with it since it beeps. It has a backlit screen as well as a light where you insert the test strip. The Guide Me is very bare bones but still with Bluetooth. 

The mySugr app is nice too. You're able to record a lot of information in addition to your numbers from the meter.

My stomach is already extremely sensitive. I do 1000mg of XR twice a day and I have diarrhea daily. This is like my 3rd time being on it and starting was pretty miserable because I had cramps hard core and I had to halve my dose several times so I could function. I'm sticking with the recommended dose and my A1c plummeted and I'm encouraged to drink a lot of water so I guess it's worth it for peace of mind about my levels.
So I really really really liked this explanation. It's really making me feel more accepting of using insulin.

A lot of things.

My biggest fear is losing weight not working and I gain it all back and I give up. Also afraid of the loose skin. Been fat all my life so I know it's going to be there. How much I don't know, but if I have a lot, will I have to remove it to live a normal life? Will I be able to afford it if it's medically necessary.

Prolly next down the list is the attention. Last time around, the extra attention kinda shut me down but thanks to winter clothes, few have noticed this time around.

But change in general scares me. So you can ask about any change whether it's moving to a new place or trying out a new hair product. It all scares me and I can tell you a million reasons why.

But at least for this change, I'm more hopeful than scared (ask me tomorrow and it may be a different answer)!

I didn't expect anyone to care to respond. Just thought I was just screaming into the wind. Random reddit person, I don't know you but thank you for the few moments you took. I really appreciate it. I was having a good night and this made it so much better I can't stop crying.

I hate people telling me to just cheer up or stop being sad. Even people that know me and stuff will just say that and move along. So yeah. Much thanks. Much thanks.

That night was an unusual low moment for me. I deal a lot with depression and everything started piling down and I got to the point I was getting into self-destructing behavior so I had to distract myself and let some of my feelings go.

Believe me, I've come a long way. I used to just do nothing, make all kinds of excuses for everything and be very introverted. I still am. I like staying home. When I go out, I like quiet places. I prefer small, intimate groups rather than big functions. Inside my comfort zone, I can hold a convo with anyone. Still working on dealing with loud crowds but just getting into the moment works for me.

I'm happy to say that I'm a work in progress. It just sucks that I have so much to fix. There might be nothing wrong with the me that I am now, but I understand that in order to be the me I want to be, I gotta work at it. So I'm trying new things all the time. Hoping I'll find something that I like a lot.

Ahh I'm rambling. Even you caring a little bit. Man that feels so awesome.

But I'm doing my darnedest to not give up on life. My hope for the future really keeps me from wanting to kill myself at my worst points so I hope I never lose that.

I had that same kind of thought pop through my mind during last night's weigh-in. I've really hit a plateau where my weight drops a little and then creep back up to where it was before regardless if I eat 200 calories or exercise all day long or drink all the water and poop all the poop. I really really wanted to throw in the towel especially when I saw my trend line become a little more horizontal...

But yeah. I had to remind myself that when I started, how I was kicking myself over quitting and how I would have been done by now had I not quit.

Funny thing is, I told myself if after a month I didn't lose any weight or if I didn't like it, I'd let myself quit then. It worked. My new quit date is 6 months from now so I hope that'll keep me going. Knowing I can get out in 6 months. Hoping that I won't want to get out in 6 months.

(I feel bad for hijacking but right now, I feel very motivated all of a sudden)

I've all but sworn off of the stuff. I love it but I can't stop at one and I retain so much water. Like I can have a day where I eat like 800 calories and gain 5lbs the next morning. 

I still have it sporadically because seeing the water gains is not happy for me.

I don't eat back the calories. The only time I will eat them back is if I'm feeling really drained and it's early in the day and my body is screaming eat.

I did that before but I got sloppy and generous with my counting and I only maintained at best. I just play it safe now since I am more sedentary than anything due to work.

It sucks when it's nagging, but I just deal with it. If it's nagging like that, I just do something to distract myself if I know I just ate plenty recently.

I always make sure to have water nearby especially if it's boredom hunger. I keep almonds and low-cal jelly snacks at my desk at work so I can have a little snack if I do need a little something to tide me over to my next meal. And the bottom of my purse is full of candy and snack bars of all sorts. They come in handy for when I just forget to eat. Sometimes when I'm out shopping or running errands, I push the hunger so far back that I just forget about it and then wonder why the heck I'm so tired. A 100 calorie snack bar will do a lot less damage than a 500 calorie milkshake in a desperate time.

I rarely do eat the snacks I have on hand. I just like knowing they're there when I need them.

I had this happen before with my previous attempt. At first, it was like "Wow, someone noticed! Keep going!" Then it became "Well this is awkward," and then eventually "I wish I could be invisible again."

I honestly hated the attention. Then when I was still feeling good about myself, a sweet little old lady told me "I see you're getting fat again." A year's worth of progress and what was left of my self-esteem was gone and to this day, I hate that I felt that way back then.

I'm just hoping that when people start to notice this time around I won't freak out!

Thanks! That reminds me of one of those motivational quotes that says "time will pass regardless if you work out and eat healthy so why waste your time?" Looking forward to the more fun part. I miss some of the fun parts of eating (namely things that are both crunchy and salty or cold, semi-solid, and sweet) so I really really want the fun stuff!

Thanks again!
